title: New Bounds for the Euclidean TSP Constant
summary: The Beardwood-Halton-Hammersley theorem characterizes the asymptotic length of the optimal Euclidean traveling salesman tour through independent and uniformly distributed random points $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ in the unit square. It states that there exists a universal constant $β$ such that the length of the shortest tour is asymptotic to $β\sqrt{n}$ almost surely. The best bounds established to date are $0.6277\leq β\leq 0.90367$. In this paper, we improve these bounds to $0.6421\leqβ\leq0.8810$.
